title: add per-hop kms proofing and ephemeral operator lease for cross-region rewraps
author: Sana Iqbal
release_notes: Introduce per-hop KMS proof tokens for safe cross-region rewraps and an ephemeral operator lease mechanism. Backwards compatible; opt-in via runtime flag. Improves auditability for rewrapped keys and reduces blast radius for operator actions.
description:
Motivation: Customers in regulated regions require both strong audit proofs for any cross-region key rewrap and a minimized operator attack surface. This PR introduces a per-hop KMS proof token that accompanies a rewrap request when we proxy or re-encrypt data between regions, plus an ephemeral operator lease (RBAC v2 token) that gates operator-initiated rewraps and administrative KMS operations. The implementation includes a small policy evaluator, a runtime flag to enable hop-proofing, an automated consent-check that ties tenant residency assertions to rewraps, and an admin CLI to mint/inspect ephemeral leases.

What this changes: - Add new service middleware (kms/hop_proof_middleware) that emits a signed proof blob for each cross-region rewrap. The blob contains a canonicalized rewrap request fingerprint, timestamp, origin-region, target-region, and a nonce; it is signed with the platform KMS key and also recorded as a structured audit event. - Introduce ephemeral operator lease service (rbac/ephemeral_lease) which issues short-lived RBAC tokens scoped to specific actions (e.g., kms:Rewrap, kms:Grant). Leases are auditable and require an approval flag or a two-step consent when tenant residency is asserted. - Wire audit/logging to include proof_id and lease_id in existing request/span tags; added a deterministic audit watermark for rewrap sequences to detect dropped or replayed rewraps. - Add unit + integration tests, an end-to-end scenario in perf-canary that simulates cross-region rewrap traffic under dedicated capacity, and a migration that adds the new audit.table columns (proof_id, lease_id, rewrap_sequence_hash). - New CLI commands: redwood kms inspect-proof <proof_id>, redwood lease issue --actor <svc> --actions "kms:Rewrap" --ttl 5m --reason "incident remediation".

Compatibility & rollout: The feature is behind a runtime toggle (KMS_HOP_PROOF=off by default). Existing tenants see no change until enabled per-tenant or at the cluster level. Ephemeral leases require RBAC v2 policies to be present; a small helper migrator maps legacy operator roles to lease-capable templates. The rollout plan in the PR description describes a gradual enablement starting with internal-only canary, then selected enterprise tenants, followed by full opt-in.

Testing performed: - Unit tests for middleware, proof canonicalization, and lease issuance/validation. - Integration tests between runtime, kms-proxy, and audit writer. - End-to-end run in perf-canary with synthetic rewraps to validate sequence watermarking and audit queries. - Manual verification of CLI commands and a quick smoke test that shows proof blobs are recorded and can be inspected. CI initially failed on a flaky audit integration test (audit_writer_test::SequencerRace) — I added a retry and a stronger mutex in the migration; CI passed on second run.

Rollbacks and safety: The toggle ensures we can disable proof emission without schema rollback. Migration adds nullable columns and a backfill job guarded by a feature flag. Ephemeral lease issuance is separate from existing API tokens and cannot be used unless RBAC v2 policies allow it. If issues are seen, ops can set KMS_HOP_PROOF=off, revoke leases via redwood lease revoke --id, and run a short backfill-without-proof job.

Changelog (high level): - New middleware: kms/hop_proof_middleware.go - RBAC subsystem: rbac/ephemeral_lease.go + lease store - Audit: audit/writer add proof_id, lease_id, rewrap_sequence_hash fields and indexes - CLI: tools/redwood_kms.go + tools/redwood_lease.go - Tests: unit and integration suites + perf-canary scenario - Migration: db/migrations/20260210_add_rewrap_proof_columns.sql

See also: Linear ENG-2408 for product acceptance criteria and SEC-919 for the threat model and design review notes.

review_comments: Markus Chen: Can we compress the proof blob schema to avoid blowup in the audit table? Audit storage is a concern for large-scale rewrap traffic.

Sana Iqbal: We include only a 32-byte fingerprint + 2 region tags + nonce (64 bytes total). The full details are stored in object storage keyed by proof_id and only the hash is persisted in the audit row. Added note in audit/writer.go and a storage TTL of 90 days.
Ravi Patel: Need a clear signal that operator leases are scoped to a single action and cannot be reused for unrelated actions. Also add a CI test for reuse attempts.
Sana Iqbal: Added reuse rejection test (ephemeral_lease_test::RejectsActionReuse) and an assertion in the lease validator.
Lena Ortiz: Please update runbooks/incident-handling.md to include steps to revoke leases and to interpret proof sequence mismatches.
Sana Iqbal: Runbook updated in a follow-up commit; linked in the migration notes.
